title: The full राम table: all 24 forms

video.title: राम शब्द रूप सातों विभक्ति में हिंदी अर्थ के साथ
video.focus: Chant along with each row (singular, dual, plural) and notice which forms repeat in different rows.

recap: Your Day 25 quiz answers didn't come in, so here's a warm-up first. W1: Say 'in the house' (गृह). W2: What is the plural of वृक्षे ('on the tree')? W3: How do you call out to Rama? (Lessons 22-25 aren't on the site yet; if you missed them, reply 'repeat Day 22'.)
idea: A **noun table (शब्दरूप, śabdarūpa)** lists every form of one noun: 7 cases + the vocative (calling form, सम्बोधन), each in singular, dual and plural = **24 forms**. राम is the model for every masculine noun ending in -a (बालक, देव, वृक्ष ...). Learn this one table and you know hundreds of nouns.
- Vocative (O ...!): हे राम · हे रामौ · हे रामाः
So the context tells you which case is meant, just as Hindi को can mean 'to' or mark the object.
**Sound note:** ण in रामेण and रामाणाम् comes from the र earlier in the word (Day 21 rule). बालक has no र, so बालकेन, बालकानाम्.
**Video note:** Hindi meanings like 'राम ने' for the 1st case are a Hindi habit; in Sanskrit the 1st case is simply the subject (रामः गच्छति = राम जाता है), and ने has no Sanskrit equivalent.

examples.meaning: Sita goes to the forest with Rama. (3rd)
I go from the village to the city. (5th)
Rama's friends live in the village. (6th, 7th)

sayAloud.meaning: Row 1: chant the whole table like this, row by row.
Today I study Sanskrit at home. (Your day: swap गृहे for where you studied.)

quiz.q: What is the 6th case plural of राम ('of the Ramas')?
quiz.why: 6th plural ends in -आनाम्; र earlier in the word turns न into ण: रामाणाम्. रामेषु is 7th plural; रामेभ्यः is 4th/5th plural.

quiz.q: रामेभ्यः can be which two cases?
quiz.why: -एभ्यः is shared by the 4th and 5th plural. 3rd plural is रामैः; 6th plural is रामाणाम्.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: सीता ___ सह वनं गच्छति। (Sita goes to the forest with Rama.)
रामयोः is the dual of which cases?
quiz.why: -अयोः is shared by the 6th and 7th dual. 1st/2nd dual is रामौ; 3rd/4th/5th dual is रामाभ्याम्.

quiz.q: Translate into Sanskrit: I go from the village to the city.
quiz.why: ग्रामात् = from the village (5th), नगरम् = to the city (2nd, the goal), गच्छामि = I go.
